question.text: A company wants to reduce its share capital by forfeiting partly paid shares. Which of the following conditions must be met?

answer.text: The company must obtain SEBI approval before proceeding
The company must first complete a buyback before forfeiting shares
Only an ordinary resolution at the AGM is required
A special resolution must be passed, and the company must not have any deposits in arrears

explanation.text: The Logic: Partly paid shares can be forfeited if call money remains unpaid, which reduces capital. The proposed reduction of capital must be approved by a special resolution, and capital reduction cannot be made if the company is in arrears in the repayment of any deposits or in payment of interest on them. The Trap: Candidates may think an ordinary resolution suffices; a special resolution is required. The deposit-arrears bar is often overlooked. Note: Both conditions must be met together: special resolution plus no arrears on deposit repayment or interest.
